assumptions: 'AI agents' means the workspace's agent tools (object kind tool); agents only act through tools
request_human_approval is the approval check the customer means; it throws until a person approves, so calling it first is the gate
'Email customers' means util.send_email; no other email statement appears in the workspace's tools
'Delete anything' is covered by db.del, db.bulk.delete (db.truncate not listed; the customer asked about delete, and truncate is excluded from this rule)
A prediction only: delete_customer_note and send_customer_email should fail the rule; issue_refund should pass. Not verified by xano policy evaluate, which I was not allowed to run
confusions: The ai_cost_and_agent_safety recipe says 'AI tools cannot delete records' via stack.statement_forbidden, and also 'deletes wait for an approval check' via stack.statement_order. These two are contradictory for an approve-first ask; the recipe does not say which to use, and nothing says how to combine them

The skill says a check's Fix note 'adds detail' but the recipe's prerequisites say to 'write one function that checks a person approved'. The workspace already has request_human_approval, so it is unclear whether an existing function can be named without adding anything

stack.statement_order 'before' must 'always run ahead'; a function that throws when approval_id is missing still counts, but the catalogue does not say a call that can throw counts as a before. I assumed it does, from the description of synchronous calls

The object_kinds param sits on stack.statement_order as a scope filter; the catalogue lists 'Scope' params as tags/except_tags/api_groups/verbs/endpoint_auth/tables/object_kinds, but I could not confirm from the catalogue whether object_kinds is accepted by every check. Parse accepted it with no warning
wished_for: A way to restrict which tools an agent may expose, or at least a check on agent tool lists (the not_checkable topic says it is not yet available)
A recipe or template with approve-first (require approval before delete/email) as its own rule, separate from the ban-deletes template
A worked example of object_kinds on stack.statement_order scoped to tools, to confirm the pattern
Guidance on whether a function that throws until approval counts as a before in stack.statement_order
why_confidence: The approval-before-delete-and-email part is checkable and the policy parses with no rule warnings, so the rule should judge what it is meant to. Confidence is only medium because I could not run xano policy evaluate, so the expected findings are a prediction; the tool-allowlist part is not checkable at all; and the policy covers agent tools only, which may be narrower than the customer wants.
